page: Google Cloud Platform c2-standard-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 3.1 GHz, the system allocates 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The processor cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 24 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512 (specifically avx512f and avx512_vnni), AES cryptography, and BMI2. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations indicate moderate single-core capabilities paired with lower multi-core scaling. The stress-ng single-core CPU test yields an average score of 1572.39, while the multi-core CPU performance registers at a weaker 4147.67. Memory bandwidth tests show 230.44 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 28.26 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 24.11 GB/sec for large-block writes. Single-threaded operations perform relatively better, with gzip compression achieving 26.8 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression reaching 10.09 GB/sec. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falls into the bottom decile at 18.77 GB/sec. Geekbench metrics align with this trend, showing an average single-core score of 1309.0 and a weak multi-core score of 2855.0.

From a resource density perspective, the c2-standard-4 offers a dedicated CPU profile suitable for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive parallelization or local disk storage. The lack of bundled local storage means all storage operations must rely on network-attached persistent disks, which may impact overall I/O performance. Given its average single-core performance and weak multi-core scaling, this instance is best suited for light compute tasks, single-threaded batch processing, basic web serving, and low-intensity text processing workloads rather than heavy database operations or complex multi-threaded compilations.
